text.title: Agency Valuation Rubric Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a normalized EBITDA base exists, whether banded comparable transactions are available, and whether this is a first scoring run or a re-score — to full application, scoring without a published multiplier map, or a halt to fix the base or the weights.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a normalized EBITDA to multiply, and is this the first scoring run or a re-score across time or across a comparison set?

branch.when: no EBITDA figure yet, or the P&L still carries owner compensation at whatever the owner chose to pay themselves and personal or one-off expenses are unstripped

conclusion.verdict: halt; build the normalization bridge line by line first — the rubric multiplies whatever base it is handed, so twelve scored criteria on an un-normalized base is precision attached to the wrong quantity

branch.when: a normalized EBITDA exists and this is the first time the target is scored
branch.question: Are observed comparable transactions available for this target's EBITDA band, or only headline rules of thumb?

branch.when: only category-wide rules of thumb ('agencies sell for 4-6x'), no transactions observed in the target's EBITDA band

conclusion.verdict: apply the scoring half but leave the score-to-multiplier map unpublished until a banded comp range is sourced; an unbounded map becomes the seller's anchor and market-rate offers get refused against it

branch.when: transactions observed in the target's EBITDA band give a bounded multiplier range

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; freeze the weight vector before the first score, give every 1-5 level an observable anchor, and split owner dependency into relationship and delivery axes

branch.when: the target has been scored before, or several targets are being scored for comparison
branch.question: Was one weight vector written down and frozen before any score was visible, and reused unchanged?

branch.when: weights were tuned after the scores appeared, or each target was scored on its own vector

conclusion.verdict: halt; re-score every target on a single frozen vector — a per-target vector means each was measured with a different yardstick and the ranking carries no information

branch.when: one frozen vector, reused unchanged across targets and re-runs

conclusion.verdict: apply, but audit the criteria set first for several proxies of one quantity (retainer share, recurring-revenue share, contracted backlog) and cap their combined weight at the weight that concept was meant to carry
